questions.stem: Two factories produce two items in the quantities given by the rows of $Q=\begin{bmatrix}10&20\\30&40\end{bmatrix}$. The item prices are Rs 5 and Rs 3 respectively, written as the column $\begin{bmatrix}5\\3\end{bmatrix}$. The total value of the output of the second factory, found by matrix multiplication, is
questions.explanation: Multiplying $Q$ by the price column, the second row gives $30\cdot5+40\cdot3=150+120=270$. The first row gives $10\cdot5+20\cdot3=110$ for the first factory.

optionRationale.1: This is the value for the first factory, the first row of the product.
optionRationale.2: This pairs the prices the wrong way round, $30\cdot3+40\cdot5$, so each price multiplies the wrong item.
optionRationale.3: This simply adds the quantities $30+40$ of the second factory without using the prices.

questions.objective: Use matrix multiplication for total value

questions.stem: If $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\3&4\end{bmatrix}$, the sum of the diagonal elements (the trace) of $A^2$ is

optionRationale.2: This squares each diagonal entry of $A$ separately, $1^2+4^2$, instead of squaring the whole matrix.
optionRationale.3: This adds the off-diagonal entries $10+15$ of $A^2$ instead of the diagonal ones.
optionRationale.4: $10$ is the trace of $A$ itself, not of $A^2$.

questions.objective: Compute the trace of a matrix square

questions.stem: A matrix $A=\begin{bmatrix}4&6\\2&8\end{bmatrix}$ is written as the sum of a symmetric matrix $P$ and a skew-symmetric matrix $Q$. The element in the first row and second column of $Q$ is
questions.explanation: The skew-symmetric part is $Q=\tfrac12(A-A^T)=\tfrac12\begin{bmatrix}0&4\\-4&0\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}0&2\\-2&0\end{bmatrix}$. Its first-row, second-column entry is $2$. The symmetric part is $\begin{bmatrix}4&4\\4&8\end{bmatrix}$.

optionRationale.2: $4$ is the off-diagonal entry of the symmetric part $P$, not of $Q$.
optionRationale.3: This is the entry of $Q$ in the second row, first column; the question asks for row 1, column 2.
optionRationale.4: $6$ is the original entry of $A$; the difference $A-A^T$ was not formed or halved.

questions.objective: Resolve a square matrix into symmetric and skew-symmetric parts

questions.stem: The system $2x+y=8,\ 5x+3y=21$ is written as $AX=B$ with $A=\begin{bmatrix}2&1\\5&3\end{bmatrix}$. Using $X=A^{-1}B$, the value of $5x+7y$ is

optionRationale.1: This reads the solution column in the wrong order, taking $x=2$, $y=3$, giving $10+21$.
optionRationale.3: This comes from an inverse with the signs changed on the wrong entries, which gives wrong values of $x$ and $y$.
optionRationale.4: This uses $x=3$ and $y=1.5$ from an arithmetic slip, which does not satisfy the second equation.

questions.stem: A stationer sells 3 pens and 2 notebooks for Rs 40 on Monday and 5 pens and 4 notebooks for Rs 76 on Tuesday, at the same prices. The price of one notebook is
questions.explanation: Let a pen cost $p$ and a notebook $n$. Then $3p+2n=40$ and $5p+4n=76$. Doubling the first gives $6p+4n=80$; subtracting the second gives $p=4$. Then $2n=40-12=28$, so $n=14$.

optionRationale.1: Rs 4 is the price of a pen, not of a notebook.
optionRationale.2: This results from subtracting without doubling the first equation, which leaves unequal coefficients and a wrong value.
optionRationale.3: This takes $n=(76-3\cdot4)/4$, mixing coefficients from the two days.

questions.objective: Form and solve simultaneous equations from a shopping situation

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): For every square matrix $A$, the matrix $A+A^T$ is symmetric.
Reason (R): For every square matrix $A$, the matrix $A-A^T$ is also symmetric.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: $(A+A^T)^T=A^T+A=A+A^T$, so the assertion is true. But $(A-A^T)^T=A^T-A=-(A-A^T)$, so $A-A^T$ is skew-symmetric, not symmetric, unless it is zero. Hence the reason is false.

optionRationale.1: The reason is false, so it cannot explain the assertion.
optionRationale.2: The reason is not true, since $A-A^T$ is skew-symmetric.

questions.objective: Distinguish symmetric and skew-symmetric combinations of a matrix

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about square matrices $A$ and $B$ of the same order.
A. $AB$ need not equal $BA$.
B. If $A$ is symmetric, then $A^2$ is symmetric.
C. $(kA)^T=kA^T$ for any scalar $k$.
D. $(A+B)^2=A^2+2AB+B^2$ for all $A$ and $B$.
Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: A is true because matrix multiplication is not commutative. B is true since $(A^2)^T=(A^T)^2=A^2$ when $A^T=A$. C is true because scalars pass through the transpose. D is false: $(A+B)^2=A^2+AB+BA+B^2$, and $AB\ne BA$ in general.

optionRationale.2: D is false in general, so this option wrongly includes it and leaves out B.
optionRationale.3: D is false, so this option is wrong even though it also contains correct statements.
optionRationale.4: This omits B and C, which are true, and includes the false statement D.

questions.stem: A trader buys three kinds of lamps with unit costs $x,y,z$ (in rupees). The purchases give $x+y+z=15,\ x+2y+3z=34,\ 2x+y+2z=25$. By Cramer's rule, the value of $z$ is
questions.explanation: The coefficient determinant is $\begin{vmatrix}1&1&1\\1&2&3\\2&1&2\end{vmatrix}=1(4-3)-1(2-6)+1(1-4)=1+4-3=2$. Replacing the third column by the constants gives $\begin{vmatrix}1&1&15\\1&2&34\\2&1&25\end{vmatrix}=14$, so $z=14/2=7$.

optionRationale.1: This is the value of $y$, found with the second column replaced, not the third.
optionRationale.2: This is the value of $x$, found with the first column replaced.
optionRationale.4: $2$ is the value of the coefficient determinant $D$, not of $z$.

questions.objective: Solve a third-order system using Cramer's rule
